title: Trump Campaign Prepared Staff for Either 2024 Election Outcome
description_short: An internal campaign email outlined staff wind-down plans if Trump lost and transition preparations if he won; Trump said he expected to win but could lose.
description_medium: Axios reported on November 4, 2024, that co-campaign manager Susie Wiles sent staff an internal email outlining plans for either election outcome. It said November 30 would be the last day on payroll regardless of the result and that, if Trump and JD Vance won, some staff would join transition or inauguration teams. Trump told ABC he expected to win but acknowledged he could lose. This documents contingency planning, not an intention to lose.
description_long: On November 4, 2024, Axios reported that Donald Trump’s campaign had prepared staff for either result in the upcoming presidential election. The report described an internal “Donald J. Trump Administrative Update” from co-campaign manager Susie Wiles. It said November 30 would be the staff’s last day on payroll regardless of the outcome and that, if Trump and JD Vance won, some employees would move to the official transition or Presidential Inaugural Committee. Axios also reported that Trump told ABC News correspondent Jonathan Karl he expected to win, while acknowledging that he could lose. Trump spokesperson Karoline Leavitt separately characterized the work as preparation for a successful transition following victory. These facts support a specific account of campaign wind-down and transition planning before Election Day. They do not substantiate the earlier TrumpFile assertion that Trump never planned to win. The Axios article was published after that August post and concerns a distinct late-campaign event; its contingency plans cannot establish Trump’s earlier private intentions. The original allegation should remain unverified and should not be presented as fact.
